bridge: Builds on D05 evidence/provenance and S01 threat models. Watch the assigned Fundamentals playlist before the CTI modules.
teaching:
ATT&CK organises adversary behaviour. A tactic describes a goal, a technique a behavioural method, and a procedure a concrete instance. Mapping should be supported by observed behaviour rather than every capability associated with a tool name.

Separate raw observation, interpretation and confidence. A process name alone can be spoofed or used legitimately; contextual evidence may support a stronger or narrower claim. Technique coverage is not a binary product checklist: an analytic may see only one variant under one logging configuration.

The provider CTI exercises use a historical ATT&CK version. Compare their answers against that snapshot, then review changes in the current version explicitly. A changed identifier or definition should not be silently treated as a learner error. Retain provenance for the taxonomy and source evidence in your analytic note.

Before the mapping videos, distinguish tactic (the adversary’s objective), technique/sub-technique (a general method) and procedure (a concrete observed use). An indicator, such as a hash or address, is not the same as a behaviour. The Pyramid of Pain is a heuristic about changing indicators, not a universal measure of security value. Record the exact observation, the technique ID and version/date, the supporting source and uncertainty. Two reports sharing a technique do not prove the same actor. Legitimate administration can resemble a technique, so include context and a plausible benign explanation.

The videos reflect an older ATT&CK structure. MITRE deprecated its Data Sources object category in v18 in October 2025; the historical pages remain for reference. Current Detection Strategies organise platform-specific Analytics, supported by Data Components. This is a knowledge-model change, not a reason to stop collecting logs. Use the current technique page for names and defensive references and record the date; matrix colouring alone does not establish tested detection coverage. The overview videos orient you; the later mapping examples and native fictional exercise supply the actual method.

Keep three columns separate: observation, interpretation and ATT&CK mapping. For example, an event containing ipconfig /all supports network-configuration discovery in the stated incident context; it can also be a legitimate administrator action. If the parent command line shows cmd.exe, you may have additional evidence of a command interpreter. The fact that a sensor is Sysmon does not itself prove that a shell was used. Likewise, an encrypted archive with a misleading extension does not prove exfiltration; seek transfer evidence. Cite the source event or exact report passage, record the ATT&CK version and your confidence, and explain why more specific alternatives are unsupported. Ask a peer to challenge the mapping before claiming coverage.

The older ATT&CK videos refer to the tactic names and count at the time they were recorded. The official Enterprise tactics page checked on 31 October 2026 includes Stealth and Defense Impairment. Use its current names, definitions and version history when completing your map; do not memorise the older video’s count as a permanent fact.
example:
Synthetic note
Observation: source event E1 records process X reading file F at09:00UTC.
Interpretation: file access occurred under the recorded identity.
Not established: malicious intent, tool family, data exfiltration.
Candidate mapping: only after behaviour meets the selected technique definition.
Record: ATT&CK version, definition link, evidence IDs and uncertainty.
explanation: This deliberately weak observation demonstrates restraint. Mapping a file read to a specific adversary technique without supporting context can overstate the evidence. Conversely, uncertainty should be documented rather than replacing all analysis with a vague label.
exercise: Create three columns: observed, inferred and unknown for the supplied note. Then complete the provider's guided narrative exercise from its linked handout before looking at answers. Record the version used and cite the exact supporting sentences.
solution: The native fixture establishes a read under a recorded identity only. Provider answers must be compared with the specified historical version. A defensible mapping cites behaviour and states alternatives, rather than listing a tool's entire technique catalogue.
challenge: For a fresh fictional report “X ran on host H; a log confirms an outbound connection, but no content capture exists,” state what is observed and what would be needed to assert data exfiltration. Propose a cautious mapping workflow.
challenge_solution: Process execution and a connection are observations under the stated logs. Exfiltration requires evidence of data movement/context beyond mere connectivity. Consult the current technique definition, cite evidence, mark confidence and identify missing telemetry.
